Treat the theorem as a conjunction of two equivalences between independently true propositions; there is no meaningful implication connecting each pair.

- For the first equivalence, the left side is the defining compatibility of `PrimeSpectrum.comap` with `Ideal.comap`. The right side is the cyclotomic norm formula: for \(n=p^{k+1}\) and a primitive \(n\)-th root \(\zeta\),
  \[
  N_{\mathcal O_K/\mathbb Z}(\zeta-1)\sim \Phi_n(1)=p.
  \]
  Hence the norm is associated to the prime integer \(p\), so it is prime in \(\mathbb Z\). The assumption \(n\ne2\) handles the exceptional case required by the available cyclotomic norm theorem.

- For the second equivalence, classify element orders in a group of cardinality \(p^2\). Every order divides \(p^2\); an element of order \(p^2\) generates the group. Thus a noncyclic group has every nonidentity element of order \(p\), giving exponent \(p\). Conversely, exponent \(p\) rules out a cyclic group of order \(p^2\), whose exponent would be \(p^2\).

- Finally, `RingHom.fst : R × S →+* R` is surjective. The general result that comap on prime spectra along a surjective ring homomorphism is a closed embedding applies. Geometrically, its image is the closed—and in fact clopen—component
  \[
  V(\ker(\mathrm{fst}))=V(0\times S)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(R\times S).
  \]

Prove these four component propositions using the corresponding library lemmas, convert each pair of proofs into an `Iff`, and combine them with `And.intro`.
